    12	
    13	## Breaking Changes (since v2.0.0-beta.1)
    14	
    15	### Remote memory and RMA
    16	- Replace `rkey_t` (a `uint64_t`) with `rmr_t`, a struct describing a remote memory region; add `RMR_NULL`; `get_rkey` becomes `get_rmr`. Code that sent rkeys as 64-bit integers must send `rmr_t` instead.
    17	- RMA operations take a displacement relative to the remote memory region instead of a remote address: the `remote_buffer` argument of `post_comm`/`post_put`/`post_get` becomes `remote_disp`. Network-layer `post_put(s)`/`post_putImm(s)`/`post_get` drop their `base` argument.
    18	
    19	### Buffers and completion status
    20	- Remove `data_t`, `buffer_t`, `buffers_t`, `rbuffer_t`, and `rbuffers_t`, and the `buffers`/`rbuffers` arguments of `post_comm`.
    21	- `status_t` replaces `data` with `buffer` (`void*`) and `size`. `get_buffer()` returns `void*`. Remove `get_scalar<T>`, `get_buffers`, `is_scalar`, `is_buffer`, and `is_buffers`. Add `get_error`, `get_rank`, `get_size`, `get_tag`, and `get_user_context`.
    22	- Rename `comp_semantic_t::buffer` to `comp_semantic_t::memory`.
    23	- Remove the `force_zcopy` argument.
    24	
    25	### Completion objects
    26	- `COMP_NULL` (`allow_posted` and `allow_retry` false) and `COMP_NULL_RETRY` (`allow_posted` false) replace `COMP_NULL_EXPECT_DONE` and `COMP_NULL_EXPECT_DONE_OR_RETRY`, which remain as deprecated aliases. Their numeric values changed, so code compiled against beta.1 must be recompiled.
    27	- A default-constructed `comp_t()` now equals `COMP_NULL`.
    28	- `sync_wait` calls `progress()` by default (new optional arguments `do_progress` and `device`).
    29	
    30	### Runtime behavior
    31	- Freeing an endpoint no longer performs a global barrier; it only drains local operations. As a result, `free_device`/`free_runtime`/`g_runtime_fina` are no longer implicit global barriers. Call `barrier()` before teardown if your application relied on that.
    32	- The rendezvous protocol (`rdv_protocol`) defaults to `auto_select`, which uses write-with-immediate (`writeimm`) when the network supports it, on both ibv and ofi.
    33	- The environment variable selecting the network backend is renamed from `LCI_NETWORK_BACKEND_DEFAULT` to `LCI_ATTR_BACKEND`. Requesting an unavailable backend is now a fatal error.
    34	- `LCI_NET_TRYLOCK_MAX` changes value (new lock-mode flags were added).
    35	- `get_rank_me_x`/`get_rank_n_x` become plain functions; `g_runtime_init` returns `runtime_t`.
    36	
    37	### Build and packaging
    38	- Network backend libraries are linked `PRIVATE`. Applications that used libibverbs/libfabric directly must link them themselves.
    39	- Replace `LCI_COMPILE_REG_CACHE`/`LCI_USE_REG_CACHE_DEFAULT` with `LCI_USE_REG_CACHE` (default OFF; not supported on macOS).
    40	- `-Werror` is only applied when LCI is the top-level project (`LCI_BUILD_WARN_AS_ERROR`).
    41	- `LCIConfig.cmake` is installed to `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI/` (previously `<prefix>/lib/cmake/`), so `find_package(LCI)` works with just the install prefix (`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, `LCI_ROOT`). Builds that set `-DLCI_DIR=<prefix>/lib/cmake` must use `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI`; lookups using `PATH_SUFFIXES lib/cmake` (e.g. HPX, Reconverse) keep working.
    42	- `LCIConfigVersion.cmake` uses `SameMajorVersion` compatibility, so `find_package(LCI 2.0)` accepts later 2.x releases.
    43	- Fix the installed `liblci.pc`, which pkg-config previously rejected.
    44	
    45	### LCT
    46	- The default PMI backend list is `pmix;pmi2;pmi1;mpi;tcp;file;local`. The TCP backend is selected automatically when `RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`, and `MASTER_ADDR` are set (e.g. under `torchrun`).
    47	- `LCT_pmi_initialize`/`LCT_pmi_finalize` are reference-counted.
    48	- Log lines include an elapsed-time field.
    49	
    50	## Major Changes
    51	- GPU Direct RDMA (new since beta.1)
    52	  - Build with `LCI_USE_CUDA` or `LCI_USE_HIP` (mutually exclusive).
    53	  - Memory-type hints `MR_HOST`/`MR_DEVICE`/`MR_UNKNOWN`; DMA-BUF support (`use_dmabuf`).
    54	  - GPU Direct RDMA for small messages. See @ref gpu_direct_rdma.
    55	- Collectives
    56	  - Add `allgather`, `allreduce`, `reduce_scatter`, and nonblocking `alltoall`.
    57	  - Nonblocking `broadcast` and `barrier`; selectable algorithms (`broadcast_algorithm_t`, `reduce_scatter_algorithm_t`, `allreduce_algorithm_t`).
    58	- Completion objects
    59	  - Add the `counter` completion object (`alloc_counter`, `counter_get`, `counter_set`).
    60	  - Add `wait_drained`/`test_drained`.
    61	  - Support user-defined completion objects (`attr_comp_type_t::custom`).
    62	- Failure reporting
    63	  - Report the peer rank for asynchronous completion failures: `peer_failure_error` (with `failed_rank()`) and `net_opcode_t::ERROR` from `net_poll_cq`.
    64	  - Use abortive teardown after network failures.
    65	- Runtime and configuration
    66	  - Add `global_initialize`/`global_finalize` and `set_g_default_attr`/`get_g_default_attr`.
    67	  - Add backend-agnostic network device selection (`device_name`).
    68	  - Automatically select the network backend.
    69	  - Add an optional memory registration cache (`LCI_USE_REG_CACHE`, `use_reg_cache`).
    70	  - Add a dedicated progress endpoint (`alloc_progress_endpoint`).
    71	  - Accept textual boolean values (`true`/`false`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`) in environment variables.
    72	- Network backends
    73	  - ibv: reserve send-queue slots for high-priority messages (`net_send_reserved_pct`); split endpoints from devices.
    74	  - ofi: add the `mr` and `all` values for `ofi_lock_mode`; enable CXI write-with-immediate; allow HMEM providers without injection support; let providers choose the address vector type; use allgather for bootstrap.
    75	- **Experimental**: intra-node shared-memory transport for small messages. Build with `-DLCI_WITH_SHM=ON` (default OFF); enable at runtime with `shm_enable`.
    76	- Bootstrap (LCT PMI)
    77	  - Add a TCP PMI backend compatible with `torchrun`.
    78	  - Reuse an already initialized LCT PMI in LCI bootstrap; use PMI for endpoint readiness.
    79	  - Add `LCT_pmi_abort`.
    80	  - `lcrun` isolates the file PMI state of each invocation and terminates the remaining ranks when one fails.
    81	
    82	## Other Changes
    83	- Add examples (distributed array) and benchmarks (`bench_am_lat`, `bench_put_bw`, `bench_many2many_am`, `bench_get_buffer_attr`).
    84	- Spack package: add the `bootstrap` variant. Fix the `npackets` and `fabric-n{sends,recvs,cqes}-max` variants being ignored for LCI 2. Reject `fabric=ucx` for LCI 2, which has no UCX backend.
    85	- Fix the declarations of `get_reduce_scatter_algorithm_str` and `get_allreduce_algorithm_str`.
    86	- Fixes for packet loss with user-provided packets, a deadlock when allocating multiple devices, double completion signals, and C23 compatibility of the vendored UCS code used by the registration cache.
    87	- Add CodeQL and downstream CI (LCW, Reconverse).
    88	- Correct the `SPDX-License-Identifier` headers to `NCSA`, matching `LICENSE` (some headers incorrectly said `MIT`). Add AMD to the developers listed in `LICENSE`.

def generate_doc(item):
  doc = {}
  if "doc" in item:
    doc = item["doc"]
  in_group = doc.get("in_group", "LCI_OTHER")
  params = []
  returns = []

  if item["category"] == "operation":
    # For operation 
    group_id = f"LCI_{item['name'].upper()}"
    group_name = f"{item['name']}"
    brief = doc.get("brief", f"LCI operation {item['name']}")
    details = doc.get("details", "")

    arguments = [arg for arg in item["args"] if arg["category"] == "argument"]
    return_vals = [arg for arg in item["args"] if arg["category"] == "return_val"]

    for arg in arguments:
      inout_trait = ""
      if "in" in arg["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[in]"
      elif "out" in arg["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[out]"
      elif "inout" in arg["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[in,out]"
      
      pos_opt_trait = ""
      if "positional" in arg["trait"]:
        pos_opt_trait = "positional"
      elif "optional" in arg["trait"]:
        pos_opt_trait = "optional"
      params.append(f" * @param{inout_trait} {arg['name']} of type __{arg['type']}__; {pos_opt_trait} argument; {arg['comment']}")

    for return_val in return_vals:
      returns.append(f" * @return of type __{return_val['type']}__; {return_val['comment']}")
  
  elif item["category"] == "resource":  
    # For resource
    group_id = f"LCI_{item['name'].upper()}"
    group_name = f"RESOURCE {item['name']}"
    brief = doc.get("brief", f"LCI resource {item['name']}")
    details = doc.get("details", "")

    for attr in item["attrs"]:
      inout_trait = ""
      if "in" in attr["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[in]"
      elif "out" in attr["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[out]"
      elif "inout" in attr["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[in,out]"
      params.append(f" * @param{inout_trait} {attr['name']} of type __{attr['type']}__; {attr['comment']}")
  params = "\n".join(params)
  returns = "\n".join(returns)

  return f"""
/**
 * @defgroup {group_id} {group_name}
 * @ingroup {in_group}
 * @brief {brief}
 * @details {details}
{params}
{returns}
 */
 
 /**
  * @ingroup {group_id}
  * @brief The actual implementation for {group_name}.
  */"""

     3	# Change log for LCI v2.0.0
     4	
     5	LCI v2.0.0 is the first stable release of LCI version 2. LCI 2 is a
     6	redesign of LCI 1.x with a new C++ interface. See the
     7	[SC '25 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01864) and the @ref tutorial for an
     8	introduction. This changelog covers changes since v2.0.0-beta.1.
     9	
    10	From this release on, LCI follows semantic versioning for the public API in
    11	`lci.hpp`. Features marked experimental are excluded from this guarantee.
    12	
    13	## Breaking Changes (since v2.0.0-beta.1)
    14	
    15	### Remote memory and RMA
    16	- Replace `rkey_t` (a `uint64_t`) with `rmr_t`, a struct describing a remote memory region; add `RMR_NULL`; `get_rkey` becomes `get_rmr`. Code that sent rkeys as 64-bit integers must send `rmr_t` instead.
    17	- RMA operations take a displacement relative to the remote memory region instead of a remote address: the `remote_buffer` argument of `post_comm`/`post_put`/`post_get` becomes `remote_disp`. Network-layer `post_put(s)`/`post_putImm(s)`/`post_get` drop their `base` argument.
    18	
    19	### Buffers and completion status
    20	- Remove `data_t`, `buffer_t`, `buffers_t`, `rbuffer_t`, and `rbuffers_t`, and the `buffers`/`rbuffers` arguments of `post_comm`.
    21	- `status_t` replaces `data` with `buffer` (`void*`) and `size`. `get_buffer()` returns `void*`. Remove `get_scalar<T>`, `get_buffers`, `is_scalar`, `is_buffer`, and `is_buffers`. Add `get_error`, `get_rank`, `get_size`, `get_tag`, and `get_user_context`.
    22	- Rename `comp_semantic_t::buffer` to `comp_semantic_t::memory`.
    23	- Remove the `force_zcopy` argument.
    24	
    25	### Completion objects
    26	- `COMP_NULL` (`allow_posted` and `allow_retry` false) and `COMP_NULL_RETRY` (`allow_posted` false) replace `COMP_NULL_EXPECT_DONE` and `COMP_NULL_EXPECT_DONE_OR_RETRY`, which remain as deprecated aliases. Their numeric values changed, so code compiled against beta.1 must be recompiled.
    27	- A default-constructed `comp_t()` now equals `COMP_NULL`.
    28	- `sync_wait` calls `progress()` by default (new optional arguments `do_progress` and `device`).
    29	
    30	### Runtime behavior
    31	- Freeing an endpoint no longer performs a global barrier; it only drains local operations. As a result, `free_device`/`free_runtime`/`g_runtime_fina` are no longer implicit global barriers. Call `barrier()` before teardown if your application relied on that.
    32	- The rendezvous protocol (`rdv_protocol`) defaults to `auto_select`, which uses write-with-immediate (`writeimm`) when the network supports it, on both ibv and ofi.
    33	- The environment variable selecting the network backend is renamed from `LCI_NETWORK_BACKEND_DEFAULT` to `LCI_ATTR_BACKEND`. Requesting an unavailable backend is now a fatal error.
    34	- `LCI_NET_TRYLOCK_MAX` changes value (new lock-mode flags were added).
    35	- `get_rank_me_x`/`get_rank_n_x` become plain functions; `g_runtime_init` returns `runtime_t`.
    36	
    37	### Build and packaging
    38	- Network backend libraries are linked `PRIVATE`. Applications that used libibverbs/libfabric directly must link them themselves.
    39	- Replace `LCI_COMPILE_REG_CACHE`/`LCI_USE_REG_CACHE_DEFAULT` with `LCI_USE_REG_CACHE` (default OFF; not supported on macOS).
    40	- `-Werror` is only applied when LCI is the top-level project (`LCI_BUILD_WARN_AS_ERROR`).
    41	- `LCIConfig.cmake` is installed to `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI/` (previously `<prefix>/lib/cmake/`), so `find_package(LCI)` works with just the install prefix (`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, `LCI_ROOT`). Builds that set `-DLCI_DIR=<prefix>/lib/cmake` must use `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI`; lookups using `PATH_SUFFIXES lib/cmake` (e.g. HPX, Reconverse) keep working.
    42	- `LCIConfigVersion.cmake` uses `SameMajorVersion` compatibility, so `find_package(LCI 2.0)` accepts later 2.x releases.
    43	- Fix the installed `liblci.pc`, which pkg-config previously rejected.
    44	
    45	### LCT
    46	- The default PMI backend list is `pmix;pmi2;pmi1;mpi;tcp;file;local`. The TCP backend is selected automatically when `RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`, and `MASTER_ADDR` are set (e.g. under `torchrun`).
    47	- `LCT_pmi_initialize`/`LCT_pmi_finalize` are reference-counted.
    48	- Log lines include an elapsed-time field.
    49	
    50	## Major Changes
    51	- GPU Direct RDMA (new since beta.1)
    52	  - Build with `LCI_USE_CUDA` or `LCI_USE_HIP` (mutually exclusive).
    53	  - Memory-type hints `MR_HOST`/`MR_DEVICE`/`MR_UNKNOWN`; DMA-BUF support (`use_dmabuf`).
    54	  - GPU Direct RDMA for small messages. See @ref gpu_direct_rdma.
    55	- Collectives
    56	  - Add `allgather`, `allreduce`, `reduce_scatter`, and nonblocking `alltoall`.
    57	  - Nonblocking `broadcast` and `barrier`; selectable algorithms (`broadcast_algorithm_t`, `reduce_scatter_algorithm_t`, `allreduce_algorithm_t`).
    58	- Completion objects
    59	  - Add the `counter` completion object (`alloc_counter`, `counter_get`, `counter_set`).
    60	  - Add `wait_drained`/`test_drained`.
    61	  - Support user-defined completion objects (`attr_comp_type_t::custom`).
    62	- Failure reporting
    63	  - Report the peer rank for asynchronous completion failures: `peer_failure_error` (with `failed_rank()`) and `net_opcode_t::ERROR` from `net_poll_cq`.
    64	  - Use abortive teardown after network failures.
    65	- Runtime and configuration
    66	  - Add `global_initialize`/`global_finalize` and `set_g_default_attr`/`get_g_default_attr`.
    67	  - Add backend-agnostic network device selection (`device_name`).
    68	  - Automatically select the network backend.
    69	  - Add an optional memory registration cache (`LCI_USE_REG_CACHE`, `use_reg_cache`).
    70	  - Add a dedicated progress endpoint (`alloc_progress_endpoint`).
    71	  - Accept textual boolean values (`true`/`false`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`) in environment variables.
    72	- Network backends
    73	  - ibv: reserve send-queue slots for high-priority messages (`net_send_reserved_pct`); split endpoints from devices.
    74	  - ofi: add the `mr` and `all` values for `ofi_lock_mode`; enable CXI write-with-immediate; allow HMEM providers without injection support; let providers choose the address vector type; use allgather for bootstrap.
    75	- **Experimental**: intra-node shared-memory transport for small messages. Build with `-DLCI_WITH_SHM=ON` (default OFF); enable at runtime with `shm_enable`.
    76	- Bootstrap (LCT PMI)
    77	  - Add a TCP PMI backend compatible with `torchrun`.
    78	  - Reuse an already initialized LCT PMI in LCI bootstrap; use PMI for endpoint readiness.
    79	  - Add `LCT_pmi_abort`.
    80	  - `lcrun` isolates the file PMI state of each invocation and terminates the remaining ranks when one fails.
    81	
    82	## Other Changes
    83	- Add examples (distributed array) and benchmarks (`bench_am_lat`, `bench_put_bw`, `bench_many2many_am`, `bench_get_buffer_attr`).
    84	- Spack package: add the `bootstrap` variant. Fix the `npackets` and `fabric-n{sends,recvs,cqes}-max` variants being ignored for LCI 2. Reject `fabric=ucx` for LCI 2, which has no UCX backend.
    85	- Fix the declarations of `get_reduce_scatter_algorithm_str` and `get_allreduce_algorithm_str`.
    86	- Fixes for packet loss with user-provided packets, a deadlock when allocating multiple devices, double completion signals, and C23 compatibility of the vendored UCS code used by the registration cache.
    87	- Add CodeQL and downstream CI (LCW, Reconverse).
    88	- Correct the `SPDX-License-Identifier` headers to `NCSA`, matching `LICENSE` (some headers incorrectly said `MIT`). Add AMD to the developers listed in `LICENSE`.

def generate_doc(item):
  doc = {}
  if "doc" in item:
    doc = item["doc"]
  in_group = doc.get("in_group", "LCI_OTHER")
  params = []
  returns = []

  if item["category"] == "operation":
    # For operation 
    group_id = f"LCI_{item['name'].upper()}"
    group_name = f"{item['name']}"
    brief = doc.get("brief", f"LCI operation {item['name']}")
    details = doc.get("details", "")

    arguments = [arg for arg in item["args"] if arg["category"] == "argument"]
    return_vals = [arg for arg in item["args"] if arg["category"] == "return_val"]

    for arg in arguments:
      inout_trait = ""
      if "in" in arg["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[in]"
      elif "out" in arg["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[out]"
      elif "inout" in arg["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[in,out]"
      
      pos_opt_trait = ""
      if "positional" in arg["trait"]:
        pos_opt_trait = "positional"
      elif "optional" in arg["trait"]:
        pos_opt_trait = "optional"
      params.append(f" * @param{inout_trait} {arg['name']} of type __{arg['type']}__; {pos_opt_trait} argument; {arg['comment']}")

    for return_val in return_vals:
      returns.append(f" * @return of type __{return_val['type']}__; {return_val['comment']}")
  
  elif item["category"] == "resource":  
    # For resource
    group_id = f"LCI_{item['name'].upper()}"
    group_name = f"RESOURCE {item['name']}"
    brief = doc.get("brief", f"LCI resource {item['name']}")
    details = doc.get("details", "")

    for attr in item["attrs"]:
      inout_trait = ""
      if "in" in attr["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[in]"
      elif "out" in attr["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[out]"
      elif "inout" in attr["trait"]:
        inout_trait = "[in,out]"
      params.append(f" * @param{inout_trait} {attr['name']} of type __{attr['type']}__; {attr['comment']}")
  params = "\n".join(params)
  returns = "\n".join(returns)

  return f"""
/**
 * @defgroup {group_id} {group_name}
 * @ingroup {in_group}
 * @brief {brief}
 * @details {details}
{params}
{returns}
 */

  * @ingroup {group_id}
  * @brief The actual implementation for {group_name}.
  */"""

     1	@page Changelog_2_0_0 Changelog v2.0.0
     2	
     3	# Change log for LCI v2.0.0
     4	
     5	LCI v2.0.0 is the first stable release of LCI version 2. LCI 2 is a
     6	redesign of LCI 1.x with a new C++ interface. See the
     7	[SC '25 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01864) and the @ref tutorial for an
     8	introduction. This changelog covers changes since v2.0.0-beta.1.
     9	
    10	From this release on, LCI follows semantic versioning for the public API in
    11	`lci.hpp`. Features marked experimental are excluded from this guarantee.
    12	
    13	## Breaking Changes (since v2.0.0-beta.1)
    14	
    15	### Remote memory and RMA
    16	- Replace `rkey_t` (a `uint64_t`) with `rmr_t`, a struct describing a remote memory region; add `RMR_NULL`; `get_rkey` becomes `get_rmr`. Code that sent rkeys as 64-bit integers must send `rmr_t` instead.
    17	- RMA operations take a displacement relative to the remote memory region instead of a remote address: the `remote_buffer` argument of `post_comm`/`post_put`/`post_get` becomes `remote_disp`. Network-layer `post_put(s)`/`post_putImm(s)`/`post_get` drop their `base` argument.
    18	
    19	### Buffers and completion status
    20	- Remove `data_t`, `buffer_t`, `buffers_t`, `rbuffer_t`, and `rbuffers_t`, and the `buffers`/`rbuffers` arguments of `post_comm`.
    21	- `status_t` replaces `data` with `buffer` (`void*`) and `size`. `get_buffer()` returns `void*`. Remove `get_scalar<T>`, `get_buffers`, `is_scalar`, `is_buffer`, and `is_buffers`. Add `get_error`, `get_rank`, `get_size`, `get_tag`, and `get_user_context`.
    22	- Rename `comp_semantic_t::buffer` to `comp_semantic_t::memory`.
    23	- Remove the `force_zcopy` argument.
    24	
    25	### Completion objects
    26	- `COMP_NULL` (`allow_posted` and `allow_retry` false) and `COMP_NULL_RETRY` (`allow_posted` false) replace `COMP_NULL_EXPECT_DONE` and `COMP_NULL_EXPECT_DONE_OR_RETRY`, which remain as deprecated aliases. Their numeric values changed, so code compiled against beta.1 must be recompiled.
    27	- A default-constructed `comp_t()` now equals `COMP_NULL`.
    28	- `sync_wait` calls `progress()` by default (new optional arguments `do_progress` and `device`).
    29	
    30	### Runtime behavior
    31	- Freeing an endpoint no longer performs a global barrier; it only drains local operations. As a result, `free_device`/`free_runtime`/`g_runtime_fina` are no longer implicit global barriers. Call `barrier()` before teardown if your application relied on that.
    32	- The rendezvous protocol (`rdv_protocol`) defaults to `auto_select`, which uses write-with-immediate (`writeimm`) when the network supports it, on both ibv and ofi.
    33	- The environment variable selecting the network backend is renamed from `LCI_NETWORK_BACKEND_DEFAULT` to `LCI_ATTR_BACKEND`. Requesting an unavailable backend is now a fatal error.
    34	- `LCI_NET_TRYLOCK_MAX` changes value (new lock-mode flags were added).
    35	- `get_rank_me_x`/`get_rank_n_x` become plain functions; `g_runtime_init` returns `runtime_t`.
    36	
    37	### Build and packaging
    38	- Network backend libraries are linked `PRIVATE`. Applications that used libibverbs/libfabric directly must link them themselves.
    39	- Replace `LCI_COMPILE_REG_CACHE`/`LCI_USE_REG_CACHE_DEFAULT` with `LCI_USE_REG_CACHE` (default OFF; not supported on macOS).
    40	- `-Werror` is only applied when LCI is the top-level project (`LCI_BUILD_WARN_AS_ERROR`).
    41	- `LCIConfig.cmake` is installed to `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI/` (previously `<prefix>/lib/cmake/`), so `find_package(LCI)` works with just the install prefix (`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, `LCI_ROOT`). Builds that set `-DLCI_DIR=<prefix>/lib/cmake` must use `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI`; lookups using `PATH_SUFFIXES lib/cmake` (e.g. HPX, Reconverse) keep working.
    42	- `LCIConfigVersion.cmake` uses `SameMajorVersion` compatibility, so `find_package(LCI 2.0)` accepts later 2.x releases.
    43	- Fix the installed `liblci.pc`, which pkg-config previously rejected.
    44	
    45	### LCT
    46	- The default PMI backend list is `pmix;pmi2;pmi1;mpi;tcp;file;local`. The TCP backend is selected automatically when `RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`, and `MASTER_ADDR` are set (e.g. under `torchrun`).
    47	- `LCT_pmi_initialize`/`LCT_pmi_finalize` are reference-counted.
    48	- Log lines include an elapsed-time field.
    49	
    50	## Major Changes
    51	- GPU Direct RDMA (new since beta.1)
    52	  - Build with `LCI_USE_CUDA` or `LCI_USE_HIP` (mutually exclusive).
    53	  - Memory-type hints `MR_HOST`/`MR_DEVICE`/`MR_UNKNOWN`; DMA-BUF support (`use_dmabuf`).
    54	  - GPU Direct RDMA for small messages. See @ref gpu_direct_rdma.
    55	- Collectives
    56	  - Add `allgather`, `allreduce`, `reduce_scatter`, and nonblocking `alltoall`.
    57	  - Nonblocking `broadcast` and `barrier`; selectable algorithms (`broadcast_algorithm_t`, `reduce_scatter_algorithm_t`, `allreduce_algorithm_t`).
    58	- Completion objects
    59	  - Add the `counter` completion object (`alloc_counter`, `counter_get`, `counter_set`).
    60	  - Add `wait_drained`/`test_drained`.
    61	  - Support user-defined completion objects (`attr_comp_type_t::custom`).
    62	- Failure reporting
    63	  - Report the peer rank for asynchronous completion failures: `peer_failure_error` (with `failed_rank()`) and `net_opcode_t::ERROR` from `net_poll_cq`.
    64	  - Use abortive teardown after network failures.
    65	- Runtime and configuration
    66	  - Add `global_initialize`/`global_finalize` and `set_g_default_attr`/`get_g_default_attr`.
    67	  - Add backend-agnostic network device selection (`device_name`).
    68	  - Automatically select the network backend.
    69	  - Add an optional memory registration cache (`LCI_USE_REG_CACHE`, `use_reg_cache`).
    70	  - Add a dedicated progress endpoint (`alloc_progress_endpoint`).
    71	  - Accept textual boolean values (`true`/`false`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`) in environment variables.
    72	- Network backends
    73	  - ibv: reserve send-queue slots for high-priority messages (`net_send_reserved_pct`); split endpoints from devices.
    74	  - ofi: add the `mr` and `all` values for `ofi_lock_mode`; enable CXI write-with-immediate; allow HMEM providers without injection support; let providers choose the address vector type; use allgather for bootstrap.
    75	- **Experimental**: intra-node shared-memory transport for small messages. Build with `-DLCI_WITH_SHM=ON` (default OFF); enable at runtime with `shm_enable`.
    76	- Bootstrap (LCT PMI)
    77	  - Add a TCP PMI backend compatible with `torchrun`.
    78	  - Reuse an already initialized LCT PMI in LCI bootstrap; use PMI for endpoint readiness.
    79	  - Add `LCT_pmi_abort`.
    80	  - `lcrun` isolates the file PMI state of each invocation and terminates the remaining ranks when one fails.
    81	
    82	## Other Changes
    83	- Add examples (distributed array) and benchmarks (`bench_am_lat`, `bench_put_bw`, `bench_many2many_am`, `bench_get_buffer_attr`).
    84	- Spack package: add the `bootstrap` variant. Fix the `npackets` and `fabric-n{sends,recvs,cqes}-max` variants being ignored for LCI 2. Reject `fabric=ucx` for LCI 2, which has no UCX backend.
    85	- Fix the declarations of `get_reduce_scatter_algorithm_str` and `get_allreduce_algorithm_str`.
    86	- Fixes for packet loss with user-provided packets, a deadlock when allocating multiple devices, double completion signals, and C23 compatibility of the vendored UCS code used by the registration cache.
    87	- Add CodeQL and downstream CI (LCW, Reconverse).
    88	- Correct the `SPDX-License-Identifier` headers to `NCSA`, matching `LICENSE` (some headers incorrectly said `MIT`). Add AMD to the developers listed in `LICENSE`.

     1	@page Changelog_2_0_0 Changelog v2.0.0
     2	
     3	# Change log for LCI v2.0.0
     4	
     5	LCI v2.0.0 is the first stable release of LCI version 2. LCI 2 is a
     6	redesign of LCI 1.x with a new C++ interface. See the
     7	[SC '25 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01864) and the @ref tutorial for an
     8	introduction. This changelog covers changes since v2.0.0-beta.1.
     9	
    10	From this release on, LCI follows semantic versioning for the public API in
    11	`lci.hpp`. Features marked experimental are excluded from this guarantee.
    12	
    13	## Breaking Changes (since v2.0.0-beta.1)
    14	
    15	### Remote memory and RMA
    16	- Replace `rkey_t` (a `uint64_t`) with `rmr_t`, a struct describing a remote memory region; add `RMR_NULL`; `get_rkey` becomes `get_rmr`. Code that sent rkeys as 64-bit integers must send `rmr_t` instead.
    17	- RMA operations take a displacement relative to the remote memory region instead of a remote address: the `remote_buffer` argument of `post_comm`/`post_put`/`post_get` becomes `remote_disp`. Network-layer `post_put(s)`/`post_putImm(s)`/`post_get` drop their `base` argument.
    18	
    19	### Buffers and completion status
    20	- Remove `data_t`, `buffer_t`, `buffers_t`, `rbuffer_t`, and `rbuffers_t`, and the `buffers`/`rbuffers` arguments of `post_comm`.
    21	- `status_t` replaces `data` with `buffer` (`void*`) and `size`. `get_buffer()` returns `void*`. Remove `get_scalar<T>`, `get_buffers`, `is_scalar`, `is_buffer`, and `is_buffers`. Add `get_error`, `get_rank`, `get_size`, `get_tag`, and `get_user_context`.
    22	- Rename `comp_semantic_t::buffer` to `comp_semantic_t::memory`.
    23	- Remove the `force_zcopy` argument.
    24	
    25	### Completion objects
    26	- `COMP_NULL` (`allow_posted` and `allow_retry` false) and `COMP_NULL_RETRY` (`allow_posted` false) replace `COMP_NULL_EXPECT_DONE` and `COMP_NULL_EXPECT_DONE_OR_RETRY`, which remain as deprecated aliases. Their numeric values changed, so code compiled against beta.1 must be recompiled.
    27	- A default-constructed `comp_t()` now equals `COMP_NULL`.
    28	- `sync_wait` calls `progress()` by default (new optional arguments `do_progress` and `device`).
    29	
    30	### Runtime behavior
    31	- Freeing an endpoint no longer performs a global barrier; it only drains local operations. As a result, `free_device`/`free_runtime`/`g_runtime_fina` are no longer implicit global barriers. Call `barrier()` before teardown if your application relied on that.
    32	- The rendezvous protocol (`rdv_protocol`) defaults to `auto_select`, which uses write-with-immediate (`writeimm`) when the network supports it, on both ibv and ofi.
    33	- The environment variable selecting the network backend is renamed from `LCI_NETWORK_BACKEND_DEFAULT` to `LCI_ATTR_BACKEND`. Requesting an unavailable backend is now a fatal error.
    34	- `LCI_NET_TRYLOCK_MAX` changes value (new lock-mode flags were added).
    35	- `get_rank_me_x`/`get_rank_n_x` become plain functions; `g_runtime_init` returns `runtime_t`.
    36	
    37	### Build and packaging
    38	- Network backend libraries are linked `PRIVATE`. Applications that used libibverbs/libfabric directly must link them themselves.
    39	- Replace `LCI_COMPILE_REG_CACHE`/`LCI_USE_REG_CACHE_DEFAULT` with `LCI_USE_REG_CACHE` (default OFF; not supported on macOS).
    40	- `-Werror` is only applied when LCI is the top-level project (`LCI_BUILD_WARN_AS_ERROR`).
    41	- `LCIConfig.cmake` is installed to `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI/` (previously `<prefix>/lib/cmake/`), so `find_package(LCI)` works with just the install prefix (`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, `LCI_ROOT`). Builds that set `-DLCI_DIR=<prefix>/lib/cmake` must use `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI`; lookups using `PATH_SUFFIXES lib/cmake` (e.g. HPX, Reconverse) keep working.
    42	- `LCIConfigVersion.cmake` uses `SameMajorVersion` compatibility, so `find_package(LCI 2.0)` accepts later 2.x releases.
    43	- Fix the installed `liblci.pc`, which pkg-config previously rejected.
    44	
    45	### LCT
    46	- The default PMI backend list is `pmix;pmi2;pmi1;mpi;tcp;file;local`. The TCP backend is selected automatically when `RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`, and `MASTER_ADDR` are set (e.g. under `torchrun`).
    47	- `LCT_pmi_initialize`/`LCT_pmi_finalize` are reference-counted.
    48	- Log lines include an elapsed-time field.
    49	
    50	## Major Changes
    51	- GPU Direct RDMA (new since beta.1)
    52	  - Build with `LCI_USE_CUDA` or `LCI_USE_HIP` (mutually exclusive).
    53	  - Memory-type hints `MR_HOST`/`MR_DEVICE`/`MR_UNKNOWN`; DMA-BUF support (`use_dmabuf`).
    54	  - GPU Direct RDMA for small messages. See @ref gpu_direct_rdma.
    55	- Collectives
    56	  - Add `allgather`, `allreduce`, `reduce_scatter`, and nonblocking `alltoall`.
    57	  - Nonblocking `broadcast` and `barrier`; selectable algorithms (`broadcast_algorithm_t`, `reduce_scatter_algorithm_t`, `allreduce_algorithm_t`).
    58	- Completion objects
    59	  - Add the `counter` completion object (`alloc_counter`, `counter_get`, `counter_set`).
    60	  - Add `wait_drained`/`test_drained`.
    61	  - Support user-defined completion objects (`attr_comp_type_t::custom`).
    62	- Failure reporting
    63	  - Report the peer rank for asynchronous completion failures: `peer_failure_error` (with `failed_rank()`) and `net_opcode_t::ERROR` from `net_poll_cq`.
    64	  - Use abortive teardown after network failures.
    65	- Runtime and configuration
    66	  - Add `global_initialize`/`global_finalize` and `set_g_default_attr`/`get_g_default_attr`.
    67	  - Add backend-agnostic network device selection (`device_name`).
    68	  - Automatically select the network backend.
    69	  - Add an optional memory registration cache (`LCI_USE_REG_CACHE`, `use_reg_cache`).
    70	  - Add a dedicated progress endpoint (`alloc_progress_endpoint`).
    71	  - Accept textual boolean values (`true`/`false`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`) in environment variables.
    72	- Network backends
    73	  - ibv: reserve send-queue slots for high-priority messages (`net_send_reserved_pct`); split endpoints from devices.
    74	  - ofi: add the `mr` and `all` values for `ofi_lock_mode`; enable CXI write-with-immediate; allow HMEM providers without injection support; let providers choose the address vector type; use allgather for bootstrap.
    75	- **Experimental**: intra-node shared-memory transport for small messages. Build with `-DLCI_WITH_SHM=ON` (default OFF); enable at runtime with `shm_enable`.
    76	- Bootstrap (LCT PMI)
    77	  - Add a TCP PMI backend compatible with `torchrun`.
    78	  - Reuse an already initialized LCT PMI in LCI bootstrap; use PMI for endpoint readiness.
    79	  - Add `LCT_pmi_abort`.
    80	  - `lcrun` isolates the file PMI state of each invocation and terminates the remaining ranks when one fails.
    81	
    82	## Other Changes
    83	- Add examples (distributed array) and benchmarks (`bench_am_lat`, `bench_put_bw`, `bench_many2many_am`, `bench_get_buffer_attr`).
    84	- Spack package: add the `bootstrap` variant. Fix the `npackets` and `fabric-n{sends,recvs,cqes}-max` variants being ignored for LCI 2. Reject `fabric=ucx` for LCI 2, which has no UCX backend.
    85	- Fix the declarations of `get_reduce_scatter_algorithm_str` and `get_allreduce_algorithm_str`.
    86	- Fixes for packet loss with user-provided packets, a deadlock when allocating multiple devices, double completion signals, and C23 compatibility of the vendored UCS code used by the registration cache.
    87	- Add CodeQL and downstream CI (LCW, Reconverse).
    88	- Correct the `SPDX-License-Identifier` headers to `NCSA`, matching `LICENSE` (some headers incorrectly said `MIT`). Add AMD to the developers listed in `LICENSE`.

def build_dicts(input):
  for item in input:
    if item["category"] == "resource":
      resource_dict[item["name"]] = item
    elif item["category"] == "operation":
      operation_dict[item["name"]] = item

def generate_binding(input):
  if os.path.exists(output_dir) == False:
    os.mkdir(output_dir)

  build_dicts(input)

  header_path = output_dir + "/lci_binding_pre.hpp"
  with open(header_path, "w") as f:
    f.write(generate_header_pre(input))
    print(f"Generated binding header_pre in {os.path.abspath(f.name)}")

  header_path = output_dir + "/lci_binding_post.hpp"
  with open(header_path, "w") as f:
    f.write(generate_header_post(input))
    print(f"Generated binding header_post in {os.path.abspath(f.name)}")

  source_path = output_dir + "/binding.cpp"
  with open(source_path, "w") as f:
    f.write(generate_impl(input))
    print(f"Generated binding source in {os.path.abspath(f.name)}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
  dir_path = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))
  input_dir =  dir_path + "/input"
  output_dir = dir_path + "/generated"

  input = []
  sys.path.append(input_dir)
  for filename in glob.glob(os.path.join(input_dir, "*.py")):
    module_basename = os.path.basename(filename).replace(".py", "")
    # module_path = filename.replace("/", ".").replace("\\", ".").replace(".py", "")
    module_path = "input.{}".format(module_basename)
    module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
    if hasattr(module, "get_input"):
      print("Reading input from", filename)
      input += module.get_input()
  if len(input) == 0:
    print("No input found. Exiting.")
    exit(1)
  generate_binding(input)

  option_t(T value_, bool is_set_)
      : m_value(value_), m_is_set(is_set_) {}  // set default value
  T get_value_or(T default_value) const
  {
    return m_is_set ? m_value : default_value;
  }
  bool get_set_value(T* value) const

    if (m_is_set) {

    }

  T get_value() const { return m_value; }
  bool is_set() const { return m_is_set; }

  option_t(T value_, bool is_set_)
      : m_value(value_), m_is_set(is_set_) {}  // set default value
  T get_value_or(T default_value) const
  {
    return m_is_set ? m_value : default_value;
  }
  bool get_set_value(T* value) const
  {
    if (m_is_set) {

    }

  resource_attr_decl = ""

def attr_to_arg(attr):
    assert "out" not in attr["trait"]
    # replace inout with in
    attr["trait"] = [x if x != "inout" else "in" for x in attr["trait"]]
    if "not_global" in attr["trait"]:

    else:

    return {

def operation_free(resource, add_runtime_args=True, init_global=False, fina_global=False):

def generate_forward_resource_decl(input):
  text = ""
  for item in input:

      text += f"class {resource_name}_t;\n"
      text += f"struct {resource_name}_attr_t;\n"
  text += "\n"
  return text

def generate_resource_attr_decl(item):
  assert item["category"] == "resource"
  resource_name = item["name"]
  attrs = item["attrs"]

  # build attributes list
  attr_list = ""
  for attr in attrs:
    attr_list += f"  {attr['type']} {attr['name']};\n"
  # remove the last newline
  attr_list = attr_list.rstrip()

  text = f"""
struct {resource_name}_attr_t {{
{attr_list}
}};
"""
  return text

def generate_enum_attr_class_decl(attr):
  enum_delcaration = ""
  for item in input:
    if item["category"] == "resource":
      for attr in item["attrs"]:
        # declare enum class
        if "enum" not in attr["trait"]:
          continue
        type_name = attr["type"]
        enum_delcaration += f"enum class {type_name} {{\n"
        for option in attr["enum_options"]:
          enum_delcaration += f"  {option},\n"
        enum_delcaration += f"}};\n\n"
  return enum_delcaration

def generate_global_attr_decl(input):
  # declare attribute struct for each resource
  resource_attr_decl = ""
  for item in input:
    if item["category"] == "resource":
      resource_attr_decl += generate_resource_attr_decl(item)

  # declare global attribute struct
  variable_decl = "struct global_attr_t {\n"
  for item in input:
    if item["category"] == "resource":
      for attr in item["attrs"]:
        if "out" in attr["trait"]:
          # output attribute does not have global default value
          continue
        if "no_env_config" in attr["trait"]:
          continue
        variable_decl += f"  {attr['type']} {attr['name']};\n"
  variable_decl += "};\n"
  variable_decl += "\nextern global_attr_t g_default_attr;\n"
  return f"{resource_attr_decl}\n{variable_decl}"

def attr_to_arg(attr):
    assert "out" not in attr["trait"]
    # replace inout with in
    attr["trait"] = [x if x != "inout" else "in" for x in attr["trait"]]
    if "not_global" in attr["trait"]:
        default_value = attr["default_value"]
    else:
        default_value = f"g_default_attr.{attr['name']}"
    return {
        "category": "argument",
        "trait": ["optional"] + attr["trait"],
        "default_value": default_value,
        "type": attr["type"],
        "name": attr["name"],
        "comment": "argument for the corresponding attribute"
    }

def resource(name, attrs, children=[], doc={}):
    return {
        "category": "resource",

        "attrs": attrs + [

            ],
        "children": children,
        "doc": doc
    }

def operation(name, args, init_global=False, fina_global=False, comment="", doc={}):
    return {
        "category": "operation",
        "name": name,
        "args": args,
        "init_global": init_global,
        "fina_global": fina_global,
        "comment": comment,
        "doc": doc
    }

def operation_alloc(resource, additiona_args=[], add_runtime_args=True, init_global=False, fina_global=False):
    resource_name = resource["name"]
    args = []
    if add_runtime_args:
        args.append(optional_runtime_args)
    for attr in resource["attrs"]:
        if "out" not in attr["trait"]:
            args.append(attr_to_arg(attr))
    args.append(return_val(f"{resource_name}_t", resource_name, comment="The allocated object."))
    in_group = "LCI_OTHER"

        in_group = resource["doc"]["in_group"]
    return operation(f"alloc_{resource_name}", args + additiona_args, 
                     init_global=init_global, fina_global=fina_global, 
                     doc={"in_group": in_group, "brief": f"Allocate a new {resource_name} object."})

def operation_free(resource, add_runtime_args=True, init_global=False, fina_global=False):
    resource_name = resource["name"]
    args = []
    if add_runtime_args:
        args.append(optional_runtime_args)
    args.append(positional_arg(f"{resource_name}_t*", resource_name, inout_trait="inout", comment="The object to free."))
    in_group = "LCI_OTHER"
    if "in_group" in resource["doc"]:

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "master", "develop" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "master", "develop" ]

jobs:
  downstream-lcw:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Downstream Reconverse
    continue-on-error: true

    steps:
      - name: Checkout LCI
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: lci

      - name: Install Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'

      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y cmake ninja-build libfabric-bin libfabric-dev

      - name: Checkout Reconverse
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: charmplusplus/reconverse
          path: reconverse

      - name: Configure
        shell: bash
        run: |
            cmake \
                -Sreconverse \
                -Bbuild \
                -GNinja \
                -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
                -DLCI_DEBUG=ON \
                -DLCI_NETWORK_BACKENDS=ofi \
                -DLCI_USE_TCMALLOC=OFF \
                -DCMAKE_VERBOSE_MAKEFILE=ON \
                -DRECONVERSE_AUTOFETCH_LCI2=ON \
                -DRECONVERSE_TEST_LAUNCHER=${{ github.workspace }}/lci/lcrun \
                -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_LCI=${{ github.workspace }}/lci \
                -DCMK_TASKQUEUE=ON

      - name: Build
        shell: bash
        # Build your program with the given configuration
        run: |
            cmake --build build --target all

      - name: Test
        shell: bash
        # Execute tests defined by the CMake configuration.
        # See https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/ctest.1.html for more detail
        run: |
            cd build
            export LCI_ATTR_OFI_PROVIDER_NAME=tcp
            ctest --extra-verbose --timeout 300 --rerun-failed --output-on-failure

+All functions here are non-blocking: they merely *post* the communication operation and return immediately. The actual communication may not be completed yet. A communication posting function returns a `status_t` object that can be in one of the three states:
+- **done**: the operation is completed.
+- **posted**: the operation is posted but not completed yet.
+- **retry**: the operation cannot be posted due to a non-fatal error (typically, some resources are temporarily unavailable). You can retry the posting.
+
+You can use the `is_done/is_posted/is_retry` methods to check the status of the operation.
+
+Below is an example of how to post a send operation and blocking wait for it to complete:
+```cpp
+void post_send(int rank, void* buf, size_t size, tag_t tag) {
+  comp_t sync = alloc_sync();
+  status_t status;
+  do {
+    status = post_send(rank, buf, size, tag, sync);
+    progress();
+  } while (status.is_retry());
+  if (status.is_posted()) {
+    while (sync_test(sync, &status) == false)
+      progress();
+  }
+  assert(status.is_done());
+  // At this point, the send operation is completed
+  // and the status object contains the information about the completed operation.
+}

+LCI offers several mechanisms to detect when a posted operation completes. These mechanisms are designed to support both synchronous and asynchronous programming styles.

import subprocess,types,sys,re
for rev,prefix in [('v2.0.0-beta.1','beta_input'),('HEAD','release_input')]:
 pkg=types.ModuleType(prefix);pkg.__path__=[];sys.modules[prefix]=pkg
 paths=subprocess.check_output(['git','ls-tree','--name-only',rev,'src/binding/input/'],text=True).splitlines()
 data=[]
 for path in ['src/binding/input/tools.py']+[p for p in paths if p.endswith('.py') and not p.endswith(('tools.py','__init__.py'))]:
  mod=types.ModuleType(prefix+'.'+path.split('/')[-1][:-3]);mod.__file__=path;mod.__package__=prefix;sys.modules[mod.__name__]=mod
  exec(compile(subprocess.check_output(['git','show',rev+':'+path],text=True),path,'exec'),mod.__dict__)
  if hasattr(mod,'get_input'):data+=mod.get_input()
 gen=types.ModuleType('gen_'+prefix)
 exec(compile(subprocess.check_output(['git','show',rev+':src/binding/generate_binding.py'],text=True),'generate_binding.py','exec'),gen.__dict__)
 gen.input=data
 print(rev)
 for item in data:
  if item['category']=='operation' and item['name'] in ['alloc_sync','alloc_cq','alloc_handler','alloc_graph']:
   print(re.search(r'call_impl\([^\n]+',gen.generate_operation_decl(item))[0])

PY

15	### Remote memory and RMA
    16	- Replace `rkey_t` (a `uint64_t`) with `rmr_t`, a struct describing a remote memory region; add `RMR_NULL`; `get_rkey` becomes `get_rmr`. Code that sent rkeys as 64-bit integers must send `rmr_t` instead.
    17	- RMA operations take a displacement relative to the remote memory region instead of a remote address: the `remote_buffer` argument of `post_comm`/`post_put`/`post_get` becomes `remote_disp`. Network-layer `post_put(s)`/`post_putImm(s)`/`post_get` drop their `base` argument.

    34	- `LCI_NET_TRYLOCK_MAX` changes value (new lock-mode flags were added).
    35	- `get_rank_me_x`/`get_rank_n_x` become plain functions; `g_runtime_init` returns `runtime_t`.
    36	
    37	### Build and packaging
    38	- Network backend libraries are linked `PRIVATE`. Applications that used libibverbs/libfabric directly must link them themselves.
    39	- Replace `LCI_COMPILE_REG_CACHE`/`LCI_USE_REG_CACHE_DEFAULT` with `LCI_USE_REG_CACHE` (default OFF; not supported on macOS).
    40	- `-Werror` is only applied when LCI is the top-level project (`LCI_BUILD_WARN_AS_ERROR`).
    41	- `LCIConfig.cmake` is installed to `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI/` (previously `<prefix>/lib/cmake/`), so `find_package(LCI)` works with just the install prefix (`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, `LCI_ROOT`). Builds that set `-DLCI_DIR=<prefix>/lib/cmake` must use `<prefix>/lib/cmake/LCI`; lookups using `PATH_SUFFIXES lib/cmake` (e.g. HPX, Reconverse) keep working.
    42	- `LCIConfigVersion.cmake` uses `SameMajorVersion` compatibility, so `find_package(LCI 2.0)` accepts later 2.x releases.

struct UcxEnvGuard {
  UcxEnvGuard();
  ~UcxEnvGuard();

  static size_t ref_count;
};

size_t UcxEnvGuard::ref_count = 0;

UcxEnvGuard::UcxEnvGuard()
{
  if (ref_count++ == 0) {
    LCII_ucs_init();
  }
}

UcxEnvGuard::~UcxEnvGuard()
{
  LCI_Assert(ref_count > 0, "RegCache UCX env refcount underflow");
  if (--ref_count == 0) {
    LCII_ucs_cleanup();
  }
}

content.text:
1. **[P1] Static installations cannot be consumed through `find_package(LCI)`.** [LCIConfig.cmake.in:8](/home/jiayan/workspace/lci/.agent-org/worktrees/feat%2Fissue-211-release-lci-v2-0-0/LCIConfig.cmake.in:8) unconditionally checks for `liblct.so`, and line 28 similarly requires `liblci.so`. With `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`, installation produces `.a` files. Configuration therefore fails before creating any targets. The exported `LCITargets.cmake` could describe the correct library types, but this config never loads it. This is an existing defect that the package relocation leaves unresolved.

2. **[P2] Installed CMake targets omit the public LCT dependency.** [LCIConfig.cmake.in:47](/home/jiayan/workspace/lci/.agent-org/worktrees/feat%2Fissue-211-release-lci-v2-0-0/LCIConfig.cmake.in:47) leaves `target_link_libraries(LCI::lci … LCI::lct)` commented out, whereas the build target links LCT publicly at `CMakeLists.txt:92`. Consumers using LCT—for example, the supported preinitialized-PMI workflow—fail when linking only `LCI::LCI`. An in-memory link probe against existing local LCI/LCT libraries reproduced `undefined reference to LCT_pmi_initialize` / `DSO missing from command line`; adding `-llct` succeeded. This also predates the branch.

3. **[P2] Static pkg-config metadata omits enabled bootstrap dependencies.** [CMakeLists.txt:464](/home/jiayan/workspace/lci/.agent-org/worktrees/feat%2Fissue-211-release-lci-v2-0-0/CMakeLists.txt:464) collects network dependencies only. Evaluating this generator with `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`, OFI, and `LCT_PMI_BACKEND_ENABLE_MPI=ON` produces `Requires.private: libfabric` and an empty `Libs.private`. However, `lct/pmi/CMakeLists.txt:45` links `MPI::MPI_CXX`, and `pmi_wrapper_mpi.cpp:23` onward calls MPI functions. Consequently, linking static LCI/LCT with `pkg-config --static --libs liblci` leaves MPI symbols unresolved. The pkg-config repair is incomplete for this supported configuration.

4. **[P2] Deprecated Spack bootstrap variants no longer request their dependencies.** [package.py:137](/home/jiayan/workspace/lci/.agent-org/worktrees/feat%2Fissue-211-release-lci-v2-0-0/contrib/spack/packages/lci/package.py:137) requests MPI only for `bootstrap=mpi`; line 140 similarly requests `cray-pmi` only for `bootstrap=cray`. The deprecated variants are translated inside `cmake_args()` at lines 147–155, after dependency resolution. Thus `enable-pm=mpi` with the default `bootstrap=auto` enables MPI without adding an MPI dependency, for both LCI 1 and 2. Evaluating the actual method confirmed it emits `LCT_PMI_BACKEND_ENABLE_MPI=ON`; LCT configuration explicitly fails if MPI is unavailable. `default-pm=cray` has the analogous missing dependency. This regression is present in the beta-to-HEAD diff.

5. **[P2] The changelog omits changes to existing public enum values.** [changelog_2_0_0.md:25](/home/jiayan/workspace/lci/.agent-org/worktrees/feat%2Fissue-211-release-lci-v2-0-0/docs/changelogs/changelog_2_0_0.md:25) documents completion-handle value changes, but omits that inserting `counter` changes `attr_comp_type_t::cq`, `handler`, and `graph` from **1/2/3 to 2/3/4**. Likewise, inserting `auto_select` changes `attr_rdv_protocol_t::write` from **0 to 1**. These values were verified from both revisions’ binding inputs and generated enum declarations. They affect numeric serialization and compatibility with code compiled against beta.1 and belong in the breaking-change list.

6. **[P3] The TCP auto-selection claim omits a required environment variable.** [changelog_2_0_0.md:46](/home/jiayan/workspace/lci/.agent-org/worktrees/feat%2Fissue-211-release-lci-v2-0-0/docs/changelogs/changelog_2_0_0.md:46) says setting `RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`, and `MASTER_ADDR` automatically selects TCP. `pmi_wrapper_tcp.cpp:187–203` requires a matched address **and valid port**, and `check_availability()` returns false without that pair. With only the documented three variables, TCP is skipped. Document `MASTER_PORT` as required, or one of the matched `LCI_`/`LCT_` address-and-port pairs.
